title: Exploring Efficient Partial Differential Equation Solution Using Speed Galerkin Transformer
problem: FNO-based models for PDE solving have key components that cannot fully leverage GPU hardware potential, limiting applicability to high-resolution and real-time scenarios. Existing implementations achieve suboptimal performance despite strong algorithmic properties.
motivation: Efficient PDE solving is critical for scientific computing and engineering applications requiring real-time inference at high resolution.
method: Speed Galerkin Transformer optimizes four GPU operations specific to solving PDEs with Fourier neural operators—algorithms that work in frequency space instead of direct space. It parallelizes matrix multiplication on thin matrices across independent chunks that are combined afterward (SliceK-SplitK-ReduceK strategy), reorganizes where transformer components like query, key, and value matrices sit in GPU memory to reduce latency, merges normalization across multiple attention heads (the transformer's parallel information-processing pathways) into a single operation, and optimizes how multiple matrix transpositions (flipping data rows and columns) happen together using strategic memory access patterns. These kernel-level optimizations eliminate the bottlenecks that make Fourier neural operators theoretically efficient but practically slow on hardware. The combination lets the algorithm approach the GPU's peak performance.
key_novelty: Four GPU optimizations integrated and co-designed for Fourier neural operators: parallelizing thin matrix multiplications (SliceK-SplitK-ReduceK), reorganizing memory layout, merging normalization across attention heads, and optimizing batched matrix transpositions.
contributions: SliceK-SplitK-ReduceK parallel strategy achieving 10.29x speedup on batched matrix multiplication
Memory layout and multi-head layer normalization fusion achieving 4.41x speedup
Batched transposition optimization with strided operations achieving 2.38x speedup
End-to-end 1.72x speedup on Darcy Flow at 512x512 resolution with 90% parallel efficiency across 8 GPUs
limitations: Evaluation limited to Darcy Flow equation; generalization to other PDE types and comparison with other optimization frameworks not discussed.
primary_theme: GPU kernel optimization for neural PDE solvers
